timeline.event: Tuomas J. Lukka writes the original FreeWRL VRML browser. Early files carry 'Copyright (C) 1998 Tuomas J. Lukka'.
Tuomas Lukka sets out FreeWRL's license intent on the www-vrml mailing list: GPL applies to changes to FreeWRL modules, not across published APIs.
Tuomas Lukka's article 'An introduction to VRML' appears in 'LJ #12/98'. Its example app.pl ships with release 0.19.
FreeWRL 0.18 is released, the first version released by John Stewart (CRC Canada).
John A. Stewart manages the FreeWRL project.
Release 0.19: large gains in EAI (External Authoring Interface) support.
Release 0.20: EXTERNPROTO support, better JavaScript, EAI working with Netscape for local files, and shared virtual worlds.
Release 0.21 with Red Hat 6.1 install notes; Polhemus Fastrak tracker integration works.
Release 0.22, which builds on a stock Red Hat 6.1 distribution.
The Shared Multicast virtual-worlds paper is posted to the site.
Shared Multicast Virtual World code v1.0 is released.
John Stewart presents FreeWRL at the Ottawa Linux Symposium. Release 0.25 adds PixelTexture and better backgrounds.
FreeWRL project registered on SourceForge (per the saved SourceForge project page, archived as index.htm).
Development moves to SourceForge (freewrl.sourceforge.net). Web pages stay with CRC.
First commit in the upstream repository history ('Initial revision', SourceForge user rcoscali).
Releases 0.26 and 0.27: texture fixes, EAI and Java bindings work, first SAI work.
Release 0.28: bug fixes, speed, better rendering and EAI, more test worlds.
Version 1.18.10; Daniel Kraft's new VRML parser is in place, with X3D (FDIS 19775-1:2004) component tracking.
The 'Townsquare' model shows real-time navigation through an large, image-heavy virtual scene is possible.
CRC Canada contracted by the U.S. Department of Defense (Contract N00244-08-P-1769) to add high-resolution geospatial 3D rendering to FreeWRL.
Wolztyn, Poland panorama (4096x823) displayed on the inside of a Cylinder. It led in 2009 to a 360-degree imaging sub-project around Ottawa.
FreeWRL-MIDI/Reason interface released for OS X; FreeWRL 1.19.2 or later is MIDI/Reason enabled.
'Using the EAI C interface' document, version 1.01.
Canada's Parliament buildings photographed for the 360-degree image sub-project.
John Stewart (CRC Canada) writes 'FreeWRL EAI Interface Design and Function', with notes from Dave Joubert.
Windows build notes: Doug Sanden and Michel Briand port FreeWRL to Windows.
iPhone/iPod/iPad build of FreeWRL/FreeX3D in progress.
FreeWRL iPhone app demonstrated at SIGGRAPH 2011 in Vancouver. The port moved from fixed-function OpenGL to OpenGL ES with load-time shaders.
FreeX3D Android app: tablet layouts, ISO 8859-1 text, user-set texture sizes.
FreeX3D: first SpotLight/PointLight/DirectionalLight work. Choice of fast or best (Phong/Gouraud) rendering.
FreeX3D release 14 on Google Play: FillProperties shape manipulations.
FreeX3D release 15 on Google Play: STL manifold and watertight tests.
FreeX3D adds the X3D CAD component (CADAssembly, CADFace, CADLayer, CADPart, IndexedQuadSet, QuadSet).
Work continues on the library, cross-platform support and the FreeX3D Android app. CAD and Programmable Shaders components are added, and rendering moves to current OpenGL.
Ubuntu build and install revisited toward a V2.0 release; OSX build used for testing shader-based rendering.
TURNTABLE navigation and a non-standard LineSensor node added.
Stereo up-down viewports added for interlaced shutter glasses, alongside side-by-side, quad-buffer and anaglyph.
Duktape JavaScript engine option added for platforms without SpiderMonkey.
Navigation, PROTOs, sound, Inline IMPORT/EXPORT and the JavaScript interface improved.
Version 3.0: server-side rendering toy, frame-rate target, pinnable menubar, statusbar options.
Version 3.1: --want option for statusbar/menubar, touch toggling, improved help.
iOS and OSX builds no longer supported; Apple once distributed FreeWRL, but support lapsed when CRC stopped VR and 3D visualization research.
No recent binary release. Users directed to the git 'develop' branch.
Version 4.0 ('Kelp Forest'): 101 more node types, plus non-spec Teapot and Effect nodes.
Version 6.0 ('web3dv4'): most of the Web3D X3D 4.0 specification working.
Version 6.1: MIDI 2.0 UMP (Universal MIDI Packet) support. Example scenes in tests/43_MIDI.
Version 6.5: GPU-accelerated humanoid skinning, with --skin F to fall back to CPU.
Upstream 'Version 6.7' commit on SourceForge develop (b3254b11e); SourceForge project page 'Last Update: 2024-04-20'.
Ascendance Open Worlds fork (maintained by Ryan Bundy) promotes its FreeWRL 6.7 line, with native Apple Silicon macOS support, to master.
Full local archive of freewrl.sourceforge.io captured (4,059 live files plus 64 recovered from the Wayback Machine).

licenseHistory.what: 1998: Tuomas Lukka's intent - GPL applies to modifications of FreeWRL modules and does not cross published APIs; proprietary extensions possible through agreed APIs.
1998-2001 docs: distributed under the GNU Library General Public License, except files under the Mozilla Public License.
Footer on current live pages: GNU Library General Public License version 2 or any later version; 'Copyright (C) 1998, 1999...2009 Tuomas J. Lukka, John Stewart and others'.
FreeWRL described as 'released under the LGPL License', linking to the GNU LGPL version 3 text (page captured 2009).
SourceForge project page lists the license as LGPLv2.
Current source headers: GNU LGPL version 3 or later; most files 'Copyright 2009 CRC Canada'; bundled third-party code keeps its own licenses. The Ascendance fork uses the same license.
The FreeWRL logo was based on the Linux Penguin logo by Larry Ewing.

examples.title: Toon Shader teapot
examples.description: The old SGI teapot with a shader that assigns colours based on ranges of light intensity.
examples.webViewerNotes: Shader parts list external shaders/toon.vs|fs first with an inline data: fallback. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Teapot without shaders
examples.description: The same teapot model without the shader, for comparison.
examples.webViewerNotes: No textures, inlines or shaders; best candidate for a web viewer.

examples.title: Fragment vs. vertex lighting - two cylinders
examples.description: Two cylinders rotating around each other, one with per-fragment lighting, the other lit per vertex.
examples.webViewerNotes: External phong/*.vs|fs with data: fallback. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Vertex Deformer (ProgramShader)
examples.description: A flat 20x20 IndexedFaceSet deformed in the vertex shader; a TimeSensor feeds the shader.
examples.webViewerNotes: Inline data: shaders. ProgramShader is rarely supported by web viewers. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Vertex Deformer (ComposedShader)
examples.description: The same vertex deformer written as a ComposedShader.
examples.webViewerNotes: Inline data: shaders. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Sobel Edge Detector
examples.description: 'Lenna' used as input to a Sobel operator for edge finding; the 512x512 image size is hard-coded in the shader.
examples.webViewerNotes: Needs ../images/Lenna.png (archived at FreeX3D/images/Lenna.png). Shader uses FreeWRL-specific fw_* uniforms/attributes; will not compile in X_ITE/X3DOM without rewriting.

examples.title: Fragment vs. vertex SpotLight - Better (high vertex count)
examples.description: A SpotLight sweeps two identical black squares: vertex lighting on the left, fragment lighting on the right.
examples.webViewerNotes: External gouraud/*.vs|fs with data: fallback. Shader uses FreeWRL-specific fw_* uniforms/attributes; will not compile in X_ITE/X3DOM without rewriting.

examples.title: Fragment vs. vertex SpotLight - Poor (16 vertices)
examples.webViewerNotes: Shader uses FreeWRL-specific fw_* uniforms/attributes; will not compile in X_ITE/X3DOM without rewriting.

examples.title: Fragment vs. vertex SpotLight - Abysmal (4 vertices)
examples.description: 4-vertex version; the SpotLight never hits a vertex, so vertex lighting never shows it.
examples.webViewerNotes: Shader uses FreeWRL-specific fw_* uniforms/attributes; will not compile in X_ITE/X3DOM without rewriting.

examples.title: Terrain - original view
examples.webViewerNotes: No shaders or textures, but 6.3 MB of geometry.

examples.title: Terrain - GLSL fish-eye view
examples.description: The terrain with a GLSL vertex shader giving a fish-eye view; a PositionInterpolator animates the Viewpoint.
examples.webViewerNotes: 6.3 MB. Shader uses FreeWRL-specific fw_* uniforms/attributes; will not compile in X_ITE/X3DOM without rewriting.

examples.title: GLSL Vertex Shader (200x200 grid)
examples.description: A 200x200 IndexedFaceSet with z=0 on all vertices, moved by a vertex shader.
examples.webViewerNotes: 2.5 MB, inline data: shaders. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Poland panorama turntable
examples.description: Wolztyn, Poland panorama (May 2008) mapped inside a Cylinder; WALK mode with speed 0 so the viewer only turns.
examples.webViewerNotes: Needs PolandPano-Turntablef.jpg (4096x823, archived beside it in images/). Tiny and web-friendly otherwise.

examples.title: Sphere-mapped Venus
examples.description: Un-attributed VRML model; an example of sphere mapping in the X3D TextureCoordinateGenerator node.
examples.webViewerNotes: References spheremap.jpg, which is NOT in the archive.

examples.title: Toon sphere (Tomas Mikula example)
examples.description: Unlinked X3D classic-encoding toon shader example found on the site (no page text).
examples.webViewerNotes: Inline data: shaders. Shader uses legacy desktop GLSL built-ins (gl_NormalMatrix, gl_Vertex, ftransform, gl_LightSource); will not compile as WebGL GLSL ES without rewriting. Geometry still loads.

examples.title: Simple cone (test.wrl)
examples.description: A default-material Cone, 'Copyright (C) 1998 Tuomas J. Lukka'; shown loaded in Firefox in Test.png.
examples.webViewerNotes: Fully self-contained; loads in any viewer.

examples.title: A-10 style aircraft (VRML 1.0)
examples.description: Unlinked VRML 1.0 file 'Translated from TriMesh 3DS model'.
examples.webViewerNotes: VRML 1.0 - X_ITE/X3DOM do not read it without conversion.

quotes.text: From circa 1999 to April 2010, the FreeWRL project was managed by John A. Stewart.
With royalty free open standards, your models will continue to render, year after year.
FreeWRL has had a long track record, is here to stay.
Development is now handled on SourceForge.net; http://freewrl.sourceforge.net. Web pages will stay with CRC.
Just got married. But working again on FreeWRL...
V0.11 - Onset of promiscuity -- we can plugin to netscape!!!
get mentioned in the CREDITS file, the coolest place on the web ;)
It is based on the FreeWRL rendering engine, of which one estimate pegs at over a million downloads.
We noticed that musicians were able to use computers with ease.
This model was significant as it showed (circa 2007) that real-time navigation through a virtualized landscape was possible.
FreeWRL is partly produced by employees of CRC, and is released as Open Source to the world community.
